children: Smiths Group shares rose after the U.K. industrial-engineering company  reported fiscal-year results that beat analysts' expectations and projected an acceleration in top-line growth for the year ahead.
Shares in Smiths Group were up 4.6% in early European trading Tuesday, making the company one of the top gainers in the FTSE 100 index. The stock has gained 15% in the year to date.
Smiths said it generated revenue of 1.94 billion pounds ($2.59 billion) from continuing operations for the year through July 31, up 1.2% on an organic basis compared with the year before.
Analysts had forecast revenue at 1.92 billion pounds and organic growth at 1.2%, according to consensus estimates provided by the company.

The company said headline operating profit was 399 million pounds, up 1.9% organically, with a margin that rose to 20.6% from 20.5%. Analysts had forecast a margin of 20.2%, according to the same consensus.
For fiscal 2027, Smiths said it expects organic revenue growth of about 4% and a headline operating profit margin of around 21%.

The group's guidance is possibly better than the market feared and the outlook for its Flex-Tek business--which supplies tubing and ducting components--is likely to come as a positive surprise for many investors given that the division is benefiting from growth drivers in data centers and aerospace as well as positive pricing trends, analysts at Jefferies wrote in a note to clients.
